title: Alloys, Stations & Tools
h1: How to Make Steel, Hepatizon and Other Alloys in a Minecraft Survival Rework
description: How to make steel, Hepatizon and Electrum alloys in Minecraft, which stations unlock first, where silver is found and why iron needs a Blast Furnace.
intro: This survival rework adds metal alloys, a chain of crafting stations and two-in-one tools. Progress comes in tiers, so it helps to know what each station is for and what it can smelt. Gilly SMP is the worked example.

items.q: What is an alloy in Minecraft?
items.a: An alloy is a metal smithed onto a base metal. On Gilly SMP the alloys are Hepatizon and Shakudo on copper, Steel on iron, and Electrum and Adamant on diamond.

items.q: How do you make steel in Minecraft?
items.a: Steel is an alloy smithed onto iron. Alloys are smithed onto a base metal: Hepatizon and Shakudo on copper, Steel on iron, and Electrum and Adamant on diamond.

items.q: Which metals have special properties in this Minecraft survival rework?
items.a: Each metal has built-in properties: gold has Fortune and Looting, while iron and diamond host alloys. This is why alloys are the main way to progress past the early tiers.

items.q: Where do you find silver in Minecraft?
items.a: Silver is an inlay found in mountains and in Abbeys.

items.q: In what order do the crafting stations unlock in Minecraft?
items.a: New stations come before the furnace: the campfire and Mud Kiln first, then the Kiln and Oven, then the Blast Furnace, the Smithing Table and the Anvil.

items.q: What does the Mud Kiln smelt in Minecraft?
items.a: The Mud Kiln only smelts copper and earthen blocks, such as bricks, glass, smooth stone and terracotta.

items.q: Why can't I smelt iron in the Mud Kiln?
items.a: Raw iron and gold need a Blast Furnace, crafted from 4 Polished Deepslate, 2 Smooth Stone and a Kindling. The furnace block is the Oven, and it only cooks food.

items.q: What are mattocks and dolabras in Minecraft?
items.a: Mattocks and dolabras are two-in-one tools in this survival rework, so one item covers two jobs. They are part of the tier progression, so check the recipes when you reach that stage.
